verdict.rationale: GitCafe documents a public REST API with its own reference page. The docs cover an OpenAPI 3.1 description, idempotent retries via `requestId`, and `409 Conflict` concurrency protection. Personal access tokens authenticate scripts and tools against it, and `cafe api` sends authenticated requests to any endpoint. The probe's 404s at guessed OpenAPI paths only show the spec was not found at those guesses, so they do not contradict the docs. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of the API, and a verified location for the OpenAPI spec.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The same description is available as OpenAPI 3.1 JSON for code generators
A personal access token lets scripts, CI jobs and tools use the REST API or Git over HTTPS as you, with only the permissions you grant.
`cafe api <path>` sends an authenticated request to any REST API endpoint.
If the response is lost, send the same request with the same `requestId` again: you get the original result instead of a second operation.
